raw.author: KenDBerryMD
raw.text:
INSULIN RESISTANCE AT 55 WAS LINKED TO WORSE MEMORY LOSS IN THEIR 70s

Insulin resistance means your cells don't answer insulin well, so your body has to run high insulin to keep your blood sugar looking normal. A regular glucose test can miss it for years.

A Finnish study followed 43 people for about 20 years. Their insulin resistance was measured in midlife, at an average age of 55. Their memory was tested in their 70s and again 5 years later.

The people who were insulin resistant in midlife lost more than twice as much on their memory scores over those 5 years, -0.92 vs -0.43. Brain scans tied it to amyloid, the plaque linked to Alzheimer's. The authors wrote, "Our results suggest a link between IR and Alzheimer´s disease."

It's observational and small, so it can't prove cause. It lines up with a 2013 New England Journal study that linked higher average blood sugar, even in people without diabetes, to more dementia.

Don't wait for a diabetes diagnosis. Ask your doctor for a fasting glucose and a fasting insulin test. Few doctors order the insulin unless you ask.

raw.author: DrNikhilMD
raw.text:
🩸 Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM): The Future of Diabetes Care

CGM is one of the most powerful tools in modern diabetology.
It doesn’t just give numbers, it tells the story of a patient’s glucose life in real time.

Unlike HbA1c, which gives a 3-month average, CGM measures interstitial glucose every few minutes, revealing day-to-day fluctuations, nocturnal lows, post-meal spikes, and overall glucose stability.

🔍 Why CGM is Superior to HbA1c in Many Scenarios

HbA1c remains valuable for long-term risk assessment, but it can mislead clinicians in several common conditions.

When CGM is better:
• Anemia, CKD, hemolysis, or recent transfusion – HbA1c is falsely low.
• Iron/B12 deficiency or hypothyroidism – HbA1c is falsely high.
• Pregnancy, steroid therapy, or fluctuating schedules – rapid glucose swings missed by HbA1c.
• Marked variability or hypoglycemia unawareness – same HbA1c, very different risks.

If a patient’s HbA1c looks “perfect” but CGM shows multiple lows or spikes, believe CGM — not the lab.

📊 The 4 Essential CGM Metrics (ADA/EASD Consensus)

✅ Time in Range (TIR) : 70–180 mg/dL → Goal ≥70%
⚠️ Time Below Range (TBR) : <70 mg/dL → Goal <4%
⚡ Time Above Range (TAR) : >180 mg/dL → Goal <25%
📉 Glucose Variability (CV) : Goal <36%

Every 10% rise in TIR ≈ 0.5% reduction in HbA1c — but more importantly, fewer microvascular complications and better quality of life.

🧠 How to Read and Interpret a CGM Report (AGP)

1️⃣ Summary View: Start with TIR, TBR, and CV. this is your control snapshot.
If TBR ≥4%, correct hypoglycemia first before adjusting anything else.

2️⃣ Modal Day Curve: This 14-day overlay highlights patterns.
• Nighttime lows → too much basal insulin
• Early morning highs → dawn phenomenon
• Post-meal peaks → delayed or inadequate bolus

3️⃣ Daily Glucose Traces: Zoom into specific days to identify triggers.
• Weekend highs? → diet or alcohol.
• Day 1 sensor variability? → calibration effect.
• Sporadic drops? → unplanned activity or delayed meals.

💊 CGM-Guided Management Strategies

For Hypoglycemia (TBR ≥4%)
• Stop sulfonylureas if possible.
• Reduce basal insulin by 10–20%.
• If specific lows occur after certain meals, reduce that meal’s bolus by ~10%.
• Persistent daily lows → reduce total daily insulin by 10%.

For Hyperglycemia (TAR ≥25%)
• Rule out missed doses or poor technique.
• Add a GLP-1 receptor agonist (Semaglutide, Tirzepatide) — improves control, reduces weight, and lowers CV risk.
• When adding GLP-1 RA, reduce insulin dose by ~20% if TIR >50% to avoid hypoglycemia.

Always correct technique and behavior before medication:
Check injection site, insulin storage, sensor calibration, and diet timing.

⚖️ Lifestyle & External Influences

• Stress: raises glucose
• Exercise: lowers glucose (watch for delayed lows)
• Alcohol: causes late-night hypoglycemia
• High-dose Vitamin C or Paracetamol: may distort readings in older sensors

🧩 Clinical Pearl

Two patients with the same HbA1c (7%) can have completely different CGM profiles 
One stable, the other with repeated highs and dangerous lows.
Only CGM reveals that difference.

💡 Takeaway

CGM shifts diabetes management from reactive to predictive.
It helps clinicians individualize therapy, prevent emergencies, and empower patients.

HbA1c shows an average.
CGM shows reality.
Always treat the pattern, not the point.

#Diabetes #CGM #Endocrinology #MedTwitter

raw.author: BoboLucyWisdom
raw.text:
如何判断自己或者自己的孩子是否已经胰岛素抵抗了？Dr. Boz提及了四种胰岛素抵抗迹象： 

1） 带小“颈”的皮肤赘生物（腋窝、腹股沟、颈部）。
2） 颈后及褶皱处皮肤呈深色、厚实、丝绒状 → 黑棘皮病。看起来像永久性污垢。
3） 脚趾、脚踝和小腿的毛发逐渐消失。
4） 过早出现白发和加速衰老。  

记住，这些症状都可以通过生酮饮食逆转！
关注我，了解更多生酮自愈路径！
